# Optional Low-Memory Local Inference Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `executing`
- Updated: `2026-10-23T18:49:25Z`

## Objective

Offer an explicit, default-off Accelerate loading/offload profile for supported local causal models on constrained PCs, with bounded resource admission, safe staging, unchanged standard behavior and measured quality/resource outcomes.

## Discovery

The user selected planning optional Accelerate offloading rather than a new AirLLM engine. Existing managed dependencies support the direction, but explicit bounded placement/staging/configuration and installed-model evidence are missing. One cohesive end-to-end increment includes the setting, owning loader, UI, cleanup and qualification; separate layer-only increments would not deliver a useful feature.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: Explicit offload adds a settings-to-worker resource decision and private model-layer disk staging; keep enforcement in the existing host/adapter/task boundaries.
- Protected assets:
  - Local user content and model integrity
  - RAM/VRAM/disk availability and finite worker capacity
  - Workspace-scoped task/staging ownership and safe diagnostics
- Trust boundaries:
  - Untrusted settings/model metadata to managed worker loading
  - Verified safe-weight files to private offload staging
  - Worker results to public task/UI status
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - Unknown/oversized budgets or unsupported placement evade admission
  - Traversal/reparse/substitution or stale ownership redirects or deletes files
  - Silent remote code/download/precision change or unsafe fallback
  - Cancellation/load failure leaks staging or disturbs another task
- Controls:
  - Explicit default-off capability and finite validated budget presets
  - Verified local safetensors and no remote code/pickle/network
  - Private non-linked owner-bound staging, immutable input model and bounded bytes
  - Preserve task fences, existing resource guard and no permissive fallback
  - Bounded path-free readiness/progress/failures and confirmed cleanup before release
- Verification:
  - Malformed/insufficient-resource/unsupported-mode and loading denials
  - Staging containment, ownership/substitution/interruption and cleanup tests
  - Default/saved-config and structured/unconstrained behavior regressions
  - Automated desktop/thin-client UI journeys
  - Matched real CPU/GPU model runs with actual resource and task-quality records
- Residual risks:
  - Actual savings and speed on the named host are unmeasured
  - Unexecuted native file-race or other hardware profiles remain pending; component tests do not qualify those profiles
  - Opt-in mode initially excludes unqualified LoRA, training and seq2seq combinations; standard behavior remains supported

### Constraints

- Planning approval is not implementation approval; present this complete roadmap for approval before product changes.
- Standard remains default and older saved settings retain behavior. No new engine, dependency/version, remote model code, pickle, provider traffic, download, overflow allowance or precision/decoding change is implied.
- Reuse the pinned cached0.5B/1.5B models for initial qualification; acquisition of another model remains separately authorized.
- Keep the current memory guard, finite deadlines, task/workspace/organization ownership and confirmed cleanup. Backend-aware estimates need measured validation; weight-placement caps are not a hard whole-process bound.
- No human acceptance task. Automated UI and installed-model tests are required. Unavailable technical profiles remain pending and prevent closure; measured failures remain failed.
- Existing functionality/security/Canvas roadmap histories and gates stay intact. This roadmap introduces an optional capability rather than waiving their failed criteria.

## Increment 1: Optional bounded local-model offloading

- Id: `optional-bounded-offload`
- Status: `verifying`
- Dependencies: None

Deliver one usable opt-in memory-saving generation profile across configuration, existing managed loader, UI and technical qualification while preserving standard behavior.

### Work packages

- **Explicit compatible option and resource admission** (`contract-readiness-and-admission`): Version-compatible settings, profile-aware model identity, fixed presets and truthful readiness/resource estimates reach the existing worker.
- **Owned bounded loading and cleanup** (`owned-offload-lifecycle`): Installed pinned Accelerate dispatch uses private bounded staging with safe load/error/cancel/unload behavior and no change to standard loading.
- **Usable setting and real model evidence** (`usable-and-measured-mode`): Automated UI demonstrates the option and failure recovery; matched installed-model cohorts measure actual utility and resource tradeoffs under prospective budgets.

### Deliverables

- Accepted scoped ADR and runtime/security/context/readiness documentation for explicit offload only
- Optional settings in owning contracts, mappers, model/task configuration and supported desktop/thin-client UI
- Bounded verified local loading/offload adapter and profile-aware model reuse with owner-bound staging lifecycle
- Focused positive/denial/default-behavior and automated UI regressions
- Source/model/input-bound actual CPU/GPU evidence, clear failed/pending profiles and updated review site
- Prospectively declared CPU/GPU precision, useful-outcome oracle, placement/staging budgets and sampled-versus-enforced resource semantics; preserve original generation and Context gates

### Verification

- Inspect the installed pinned supplier CPU+disk/meta/safetensors path, largest/tied/no-split layers, buffers, secondary state-dict temporary creation and teardown restoration before implementation. Deny unsupported all-disk maps, source/index drift and unknown resource observations; max_memory is not a disk/process quota.
- Focused runtime contract/mapper/request-builder, resource admission, profile cache identity, staging/cleanup, local generation and constrained-decoder tests per chunk.
- Prove old-worker capability denial, profile-aware model reuse, shared-generator/input/staging leases, aggregate quotas, safe selected-path teardown and queued-versus-running cancellation acknowledgements. Cover failure/interruption/cleanup retry and unrelated task/sibling preservation.
- Automated desktop/thin-client option, round-trip, generation, denial and cancellation/retry journeys with useful task assertions.
- Prospectively freeze mode/prompt/schema/device/dtype/resource settings before actual installed-model runs; preserve all old and new failures and separately reviewed raw bindings.
- After this sole increment is fully implemented run test:all and relevant docs/architecture/agent/control-plane/roadmap gates and affected builds once, then exact candidate independent review. Run security:dependencies only if relevant dependency/build inputs actually change.

### Rollback

Disable and withdraw only the opt-in profile and its configuration/UI; preserve standard loading behavior, immutable model inputs, owner-bound cleanup and failed evidence. Never restore implicit offload, unsafe remote code, overflow or deletion behavior.

### Excluded

- AirLLM/new generation engine, dependency/version change, automatic acquisition or new model download
- Training, Context embedding, quantization/precision changes, unqualified LoRA/seq2seq offload, model-quality claims from parameter count
- Whole-system memory reclamation, termination of user applications, implicit overflow or a hard total-process guarantee from library max_memory
- Human acceptance tests, public hosting, production rollout or retroactive closure/threshold changes of other roadmaps
- Untested operating systems/hardware; native filesystem race/ACL guarantees remain separately qualified rather than inferred from cooperative staging tests
- Immediate running dataset-preparation cancellation, shared-worker termination, child-per-task topology, new kernel process-quota design or a product hard-memory guarantee
